title: Camea Mosaic Builder project file
description: THE PROJECT FILE IS A GROUND-TRUTH DOCUMENT WITH EXTRA KEYS. One file, two uses: the app round-trips it, and analysis/benchmark/score.py scores it UNCHANGED. score.load_gt() reads doc['tiles'][k]['status'] == 'anchor' plus x/y, and falls back to doc['tolerance_px']['region_default'] for a missing per-tile r. Every key those two lines need is REQUIRED below. Everything else is additive and score.py ignores it. Keep it that way: a project the scorer cannot read is a project that cannot be checked. ORIENTATION: every position in this file is the TOP-LEFT CORNER of the tile (never the centre; anything drawing a centre adds +256), in px, in the 180-degree-FLIPPED display frame (XML ax=-1, ay=-1) that every prior Camea position, every SWIM dx/dy and all three ground truths live in.

schema_version.description: Bump only on a breaking change. A reader that does not recognise the value must refuse the file, not guess.

dataset.description: The acquisition directory's name. Used to REFUSE loading a project into the wrong session.

data_dir.description: Absolute path to the acquisition directory. Informational only; NEVER written to, and a project must still open if the path has moved (the user re-points it).

tile_px.description: 512x512 is hard-coded through t33.TILE, t27.H/W, mosaic/io.py and excluded.py. A different tile size is not supported.

created.description: ISO-8601 date or datetime of first save.

modified.description: ISO-8601 UTC of the last save.

trial_range.description: [lo, hi] INCLUSIVE — the acquisition run this project covers. The load guard compares this (and `dataset`) against the open session and REFUSES a mismatch. Pass 2's autosave once silently overwrote pass 1's ground-truth records; that hole stays shut.

pass_split.description: The LAST TRIAL OF PASS 1. t33 hard-partitions on `t <= pass_split`. This is the one number the placement method cannot measure for itself — it is a fact about the acquisition. The app MEASURES it from log.txt (the largest interior inter-trial time gap, ignoring the block's first step) and lets the user override. null = a single-pass run (use t27, not t33).

gaps.description: DERIVED, and it MUST be recomputed on every change to the excluded set (excluded.gaps / t33.breaks). Consecutive pairs in the trial list that are NOT one acquisition step apart, because an excluded snapshot sits between them. The serpentine one-axis step prior does NOT hold across these. A build that assumes them away silently places the whole tail wrong.

coordinates.description: A human-readable statement of the frame. Written verbatim so nobody has to guess later.
coordinates.default: RELATIVE. Tile TOP-LEFT in px, measured FROM `origin_trial` at (0,0), in the vscope-displayed (180deg-flipped) frame. Absolute position is meaningless; a scorer must slide a build onto this with a CONSENSUS translation before measuring.

origin_trial.description: The trial pinned at (0,0). The app writes min(anchored trials). Positions are normalised on save so that this tile is exactly [0.0, 0.0] — matching analysis/ground_truth/.

tolerance_px.description: REQUIRED BY score.load_gt: it uses tolerance_px.region_default as the fallback per-tile `r`. Keep the same three keys the existing ground truths use.

grading.description: The 10 px criterion. Failure on this data is BINARY — a tile is sub-pixel right or hundreds of px wrong — so 10 px costs nothing and 100 % is a fair target.

unusable_tiles.description: Every trial the USER excluded. Mirrors `tiles[*].status == 'excluded'`. Kept as a flat list because that is what the existing ground truths carry. ⛔ The app ships with NO exclusion list of its own (his ruling, 2026-07-14): the only things that exclude a frame are the human, in the session, or a project file he loaded. THIS FILE IS THE APP'S ENTIRE MEMORY — it is what makes a session resumable.

run.description: How the run was chosen, kept so the choice is auditable.

examples: longest contiguous block of Snapshot trials

n_trials.description: The USABLE count. State the denominator on every number: 156 / 156 / 312.

cursor.description: The trial currently under judgement in the sweep. Restores the sweep exactly where the user left it.

tone.description: The GLOBAL tone-mapping window in force. Display only — it NEVER touches the matcher. A per-tile stretch is forbidden: it makes overlapping tiles disagree in brightness and destroys the Difference-mode check the whole verification loop depends on.

blank_scan.description: What the BLANK measure said. Blanks are REFUSED by the matcher (two blank frames 136 trials apart correlate +0.43 at zero shift — they share fixed-pattern SENSOR structure, which does not move with the stage, so they register confidently and WRONGLY). Blur is NOT judged here and must never be.

measure.const: std of DoG(sigma=3, sigma=30) of the flipped frame

accepted.description: Did the user accept the recommendation? The scan RECOMMENDS; it never auto-rejects.

build.description: The machine build this sweep was seeded from. null = the user placed from scratch, and this document is then an INDEPENDENT truth (see provenance).

config.description: t33.Config as a plain dict. NOTE: t33's own info['config'] is NOT JSON-serializable (it nests a t27.Config object) and json.dumps CRASHES on it. Serialize with default=lambda o: vars(o).

info.description: t33's info dict, made JSON-safe. Includes runs, cuts, margins, min_margin, run_origins, pass1_max_dev.

positions.description: THE MACHINE'S ANSWER, untouched — kept so the QC report can say exactly what the human changed, and so a corrupted sweep can be rolled back to it. {"<trial>": [x, y]}.

provenance.description: MANDATORY, AND NOT DECORATION. Pass 1's ground truth got tiles 128/129/130/148 WRONG precisely because it was seeded from a build and the human deferred to it — caught only because pass 2 was later authored blind. A verification UI that shows the machine's answer and lets a human click 'accept' is structurally that same hazard. This project has ALREADY destroyed one benchmark by overwriting it with an algorithm's output, after which that algorithm scored 100 % by construction. Stamp the truth about where these numbers came from into the file itself.

workflow.description: 'machine-seeded verification sweep' = a build ran and the human confirmed/corrected it. 'hand placement from scratch' = no build was ever loaded.

seeded_from.description: null iff workflow == 'hand placement from scratch'.

independent_of_method.description: TRUE only when seeded_from is null. When false, this document MUST NEVER be used to score the method that produced it — the score would be 100 % by construction, and the benchmark could no longer detect its own errors.

warning.description: REQUIRED whenever independent_of_method is false. Omit it only when the document is genuinely independent.
warning.default: NOT AN INDEPENDENT GROUND TRUTH. Every position here started as a machine build's output and was confirmed or corrected by a human who could see it. It MUST NEVER be used to score that method or any method derived from it — the score would be 100 % by construction. This project has already destroyed one benchmark exactly this way.

human_edits.description: The honest record of what the human actually did. Also the QC report's headline.

accepted_unchanged.description: anchored at exactly the machine's position (moved < 0.5 px)

unverified.description: placed but never judged — Space without a decision

rescued.description: tiles the solver could not place, that the human placed

scale.description: PIXELS ONLY, FOR NOW. The MEA grid pitch measures 13.805 px in pass 2 but 14.15 px in pass 1 — a 2.5 % magnification difference between the passes that is NOT YET RESOLVED (app/SCALE.md). Never put a single scale bar on a figure spanning both passes: at best it is right for one pass and 2.5 % wrong for the other.

audits.description: Optional. Free-form audit records, matching the existing ground truths' shape.

tiles.description: ⭐ THE DOCUMENT. Keys are TRIAL NUMBERS AS DECIMAL STRINGS, unpadded ('11', not '011') — JSON has no integer keys. One entry per trial in the run, INCLUDING the excluded ones (so the file records why a trial is missing rather than losing it).

tile.description: One tile. `status` is the GROUND-TRUTH-COMPATIBLE field that benchmark/score.py reads; `state` is the APP's field. They are two spellings of the same fact and the app writes BOTH, so no reader ever has to reverse-map. On load: `state` wins if present, else derive it from `status` ('anchor'->anchored, 'excluded'->excluded, anything else->unverified if x/y are non-null, else unplaced). Unknown keys are PRESERVED VERBATIM through a round-trip — the bench's gtDoc() does this deliberately, and a lossy round-trip would quietly destroy a hand-written note.

status.description: ⛔ score.load_gt() KEEPS ONLY status == 'anchor'. That is the point: an 'unverified' tile is placed but NOT human-certified, so it must not be scored and must not inflate a denominator. 'anchor' <-> state 'anchored' (note the spelling difference: the existing ground truths say 'anchor', so the wire format says 'anchor').

state.description:
THE APP'S TILE STATE MACHINE. Exactly four states; see app/API.md §2 for the complete transition table.
  anchored   — the user pressed A. Ground truth. Part of the anchor field every later tile is judged against. Drawn solid, full opacity, BOTTOM layer.
  unverified — the user pressed Space without deciding. PLACED, drawn dimmer (55 % + dashed outline), NOT part of the anchor field, and it DOES NOT BLOCK PROGRESS. Deferring a hard tile must never stall the sweep.
  unplaced   — no position yet (not reached, or the solver could not place it). In the queue / rescue list.
  excluded   — the user pressed E. Not drawn, not matched, not rendered, not exported.

x.description: TOP-LEFT corner, px. null iff state is 'excluded' or 'unplaced'. NOT the centre.

y.description: TOP-LEFT corner, px. null iff state is 'excluded' or 'unplaced'.

r.description: Per-tile scoring tolerance in px. score.load_gt falls back to tolerance_px.region_default when absent. The existing ground truths write 96 on anchors and 256 on excluded rows; do the same.

source.description: How this position was arrived at. Free text, but prefer these.
examples: t33 build, corrected by hand + snapped against the anchor composite
hand-dragged + snapped against the anchor composite
hand-dragged (no snap — blank tile, matcher refused)

machine.description: What the BUILD said, before the human touched it: [x, y], or null if the solver never placed it. Kept per tile so the QC report and the provenance stamp are derivable from this file alone.

moved_px.description: DERIVED: |final - machine|. 0 (or < 0.5) = accepted unchanged. null if there was no machine position.

ncc.description: The masked NCC of this tile against the anchor composite at its final position, when one was measured. Evidence, not a verdict.

margin.description: best - second NCC from the ranked candidate list. ⚠️ A THIN MARGIN (< 0.10) IS THE SIGNATURE OF A SURVIVING ALIAS — the shipped build's worst run margin is 0.081 against a ~0.47 typical. Flag it; never hide it.

n_anchors.description: How many tiles were in the anchor field when this tile was matched. APERTURE IS EVERYTHING: at n_anchors = 1 this was a tile-PAIR match, whose exact-NCC argmax is >20 px wrong 5 % of the time at scores up to 0.760. Record it so the evidence can be re-read honestly.

blank.description: MEASURED: below the band-passed-std threshold. The matcher REFUSES these — it does not score them.

unusable_reason.description: Two channels, and they are different kinds of claim: 'blank' is MEASURED, 'blurry' is HUMAN-ASSERTED. No automatic measure reproduces the blur call — do not let one overwrite it.

excluded.description: Legacy mirror of status == 'excluded'. Written for compatibility with the existing ground truths.

note.description: The user's free text. PRESERVED VERBATIM across a round-trip.

last_xy.description: The position this tile had before it was excluded, so un-excluding restores it instead of losing it. Never read by anything but the app.

judged_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC of the A/E press. The sweep's audit trail.

allOf.description: A placed tile has a position; an unplaced/excluded one does not. This is the invariant the whole state machine rests on.
status and state must agree. anchored<->anchor is the only spelling difference.

examples.coordinates: RELATIVE. Tile TOP-LEFT in px, measured FROM `origin_trial` at (0,0), in the vscope-displayed (180deg-flipped) frame. Absolute position is meaningless; a scorer must slide a build onto this with a CONSENSUS translation before measuring.

blank_scan.measure: std of DoG(sigma=3, sigma=30) of the flipped frame

provenance.warning: NOT AN INDEPENDENT GROUND TRUTH. Every position here started as a machine build's output and was confirmed or corrected by a human who could see it. It MUST NEVER be used to score that method or any method derived from it — the score would be 100 % by construction. This project has already destroyed one benchmark exactly this way.

127.source: t33 build, corrected by hand + snapped against the anchor composite

214.note: thin margin — come back to this one

284.note: Too out of focus to register (excluded by the user, by eye). Has light and contrast but no SHARP detail to lock a match onto. No automatic sharpness measure flags it — which is why the human call is the one that counts.

304.note: Near-featureless glare. What two blank frames share is fixed-pattern SENSOR structure, which does not move with the stage — so they correlate at zero shift no matter where the microscope was. The matcher REFUSES it.
